name: Cave Without a Name
dates: Year-round, guided tours daily; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas
customer: Families, geology fans, live music listeners
unique: A living limestone cavern eleven miles northeast of Boerne, where an hour-long guided route covers six formation rooms and a quarter mile of trail at a constant 66 degrees. The cave also hosts concerts underground.
buzz: The standard tour is the essential first visit, while the concert calendar gives repeat visitors a reason to return. Tours are limited, so reserve ahead and arrive 15 to 20 minutes early for check-in.

name: Cibolo Nature Center and Herff Farm
dates: Nature center trails daily, dawn to dusk; Herff Farm Saturdays, 9 AM to 1 PM
unique: More than six miles of free trails cross five ecosystems, from Cibolo Creek and live oak woodland to a spring-fed marsh with an accessible boardwalk. Nearby Herff Farm adds a historic homestead, community gardens and a Saturday farmers market.
buzz: The full trail loop takes about two hours, but shorter creek and marsh walks make an easy morning. Saturday is the community day, when Herff Farm opens its gardens and trails with the market.

name: Flat Rock Ranch
dates: January through October, sunup to sundown; closed November and December
unique: A private Hill Country ranch with 34 miles of cross-country and Texas-style enduro trails. Riders get rocky ranch country rather than a paved park loop, and trail runners are welcome when they yield to bikes.
buzz: This is a riding destination first, not a hiking preserve. Everyone must pay and sign a waiver, helmets are required, and the event calendar matters because races can close the trails to daily riding.

name: Comfort Historic District and Treue der Union Monument
dates: Year-round, self-guided outdoors; archives Tuesday 9 AM to noon and Saturday 10 AM to noon and 1 to 3 PM
customer: Architecture walkers, Civil War students, German-Texan history readers
unique: A compact German freethinker settlement where most of downtown is National Register listed. High Street links the Freethinkers memorial, the 1854 Faltin House and the 1866 Treue der Union obelisk over the graves of German-Texan Unionists killed after the Battle of the Nueces.
buzz: Do not stop at the monument and leave. Walk High Street and the surrounding blocks for the 1880 Ingenhuett Faust Hotel, the 1892 German Evangelical Church and dozens of historical markers, then check the foundation for its occasional docent-assisted tours.

name: Boerne Village Band Abendkonzerte
dates: Selected Tuesday evenings in June and July, 7:30 to 9 PM
customer: Music listeners, dancers, families, German-Texan history fans
unique: Free evening concerts on Main Plaza by a band organized in 1860 and recognized as the oldest continuously playing German band outside Germany. Traditional songs, storytelling and dances such as the Herr Schmidt and Chicken Dance turn the plaza into a participatory village evening.
buzz: Regulars bring lawn chairs, blankets and picnic baskets, and children play on the lawn while the band performs. Check the current Abendkonzert schedule before building a trip around it, since concerts occur only on selected summer dates.

name: The AgriCultural Museum and Arts Center
dates: Saturdays, 10 AM to 4 PM; bluegrass jams second and fourth Saturdays, 11 AM to 1 PM
company: The AgriCultural Museum and Arts Center
customer: Families, makers, tractor fans, bluegrass players
unique: Five acres of working rural history with a blacksmith shop, woodworking shop, pioneer house and a red barn full of tractors, engines, wagons and farm implements. Blacksmiths demonstrate every Saturday rather than leaving the tools behind glass.
buzz: Second and fourth Saturdays add free bluegrass jams, with musicians invited to bring an instrument and listeners welcome with a lawn chair. Tractor pulls, blacksmith classes and seasonal events reward checking the calendar before a visit.

name: Cibolo Creek Brewing Co.
cost: $4 half pints, $7.50 imperial pints, $13 five-beer flights
dates: Year-round, Sunday, Monday and Wednesday through Saturday; closed Tuesdays
customer: Craft beer drinkers, local food fans, casual runners
unique: A family-owned brewpub in Boerne's former post office, where the Mazour and Wolosin families connect house beers to local history, landscape and people. Farm-sourced pub food, patio music and a weekly beer run club make it a neighborhood institution rather than a taproom stop.
buzz: Boerne Blonde is the house bestseller, but the five-beer flight is the efficient way to explore the current taps. The menu is part of the draw, with locally sourced ingredients and mains that go beyond standard brewery snacks.
